shape_hint: A flat round annular washer (disc with a concentric round hole), uniform thickness, flat both faces; outer diameter about 2x the hole diameter (OD roughly 2.3x bolt size for 1/4, 2x for 1 in). Hardened steel, typically stamped with a maker mark on one face.

role_map.d_nom_note: nominal washer size = bolt nominal diameter in inches
role_map.d1: hole (inside) diameter, nominal = lower limit; tolerance -0/+0.032 (<1 in), -0/+0.063 (1 to 3 in), -0/+0.125 (>3 in)
role_map.d2: outside diameter, nominal; tolerance +/-0.032 (<1 in), +/-0.063 (1 to 3 in), +/-0.125 (>3 in)

notes: ASTM F436 Type 1 circular, inch only; the metric F436M table is a separate standard and is not included. Extra-thick (structural, 'HVY') washers exist from 1/2 up with T 0.305-0.375 (0.313-0.375 for 2-1/2 and up) but are not in the table. Tolerance rule (hole -0/+; OD +/-) is in role_map. Sizes 1-5/8 and 1-7/8 are stocked by some vendors but are not F436 nominal sizes. SAE pattern note: F436 OD is the 'SAE' (narrow) pattern, NOT USS.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched 10 URLs live (haydon, jhbotts, torqbolt, portland, baden, wrought, calfast, mondial, asmc, globalsupply pdf (not parsed, excluded)) + albany. Parsed all HTML tables with python (own sup/sub-fraction fix for portland). Matrix 24 rows x 4 cols (d1,d2,h_min,h_max) x 9 sources (haydon/jhbotts merged), tiers A=explicit decimal, B=fraction equal within 0.001, C=derived midpoint of min/max (not counted). Every record value matched the majority; dissenters were individually explained (haydon 1-3/4 d2 3.25 and 3-3/4 d1 3.975 and h_min 0.34 for >=2-1/4 = typos/footnote C; baden 1 & 1-1/8 d1; calfast 1/2 h_min 0.122 and 1-1/8 d1; mondial 1-1/4..1-1/2 d1). Support (A+B clusters, PDF and C excluded): d1 >=3 everywhere (1/4-7/16 and 3-3/4 = exactly 3), h_min/h_max >=3 everywhere, d2 >=3 everywhere EXCEPT 1/4, 5/16, 3/8, 7/16 (haydon + baden = 2) and 9/16 (haydon + asmc = 2). Physical sanity (d2>d1, monotone, h_max>=h_min, tolerance rule vs torqbolt limits) fine.
problems: d2 (OD) for 1/4, 5/16, 3/8, 7/16 has only 2 counted clusters (haydon decimal + baden fraction); producer's 3rd was the globalsupply vendor PDF (not allowed). torqbolt/wrought give only OD min/max; midpoint = d2 in every row (0 mismatches) but is arithmetic, not a published number. If the lead accepts midpoint-of-limits as the nominal, these 5 rows pass with exactly 3.
d2 for 9/16 has haydon + asmc = 2 explicit (+torqbolt midpoint); d1/h_min/h_max for 9/16 = 3 (haydon, torqbolt, asmc) so only d2 breaks the row.

Inch fraction sources (portland, baden, calfast, mondial) carry d1/d2 as fractions (e.g. 17/32, 1-15/32), not as the standard's 3-decimal numbers; they are counted as equal only at |diff|<0.001. 3/4 d2 = 1.468 (ASTM prints truncated value) vs 1-15/32 = 1.46875: counted at tolerance 0.00075 only. With zero tolerance the d2 column would drop to <=2 in all rows.
d2 rows 2, 2-1/4, 2-1/2, 2-3/4 have exactly 3 clusters (haydon + portland + baden fractions); rows 3-1/4..4 d1/d2 also rest on exactly 3 (d1 3-3/4: torqbolt + portland + baden, haydon typo 3.975).
h_min for 2-1/4..4 = 0.24: haydon shows 0.34 (footnote C typo); 3-1/4..4 rest on exactly 3 (torqbolt, portland, baden), 2-1/4..3 on 4 (+wrought).
d1 is the hole nominal = ID min (tolerance -0/+): read from torqbolt/wrought 'min' column and haydon 'Nominal'; consistent with the standard's tolerance table, not inferred by magnitude.
Row label convention fine (bolt size in fractions, unique); F436M metric not mixed in; extra-thick and clipped variants excluded.
Concretecalculate page lists 1/2 thickness 0.097-0.121 (wrong, dissenter); AFT table uses a different convention (not used).
